final.summary: Outfall flow exceeded treated flow by a large volume while outfall pH stayed near neutral and conductivity stayed low, then both recovered. Power matched the expected load for the inflow, showing aeration ran. Adding water to the outfall means the outfall readings no longer represent the treated effluent alone and needs human judgment.

explanations.label: Normal operation: batch wastewater treated through ETP
Bypass: untreated wastewater sent around ETP to outfall
Dilution: groundwater added to outfall, masking effluent
Meter fault: outfall or inflow meter error explains excess

key_evidence.why: Outfall exceeded treated flow by 133.8 m3 beyond tolerance, with tank balance within tolerance, showing extra water entered via outfall route.
Conductivity stayed low around 4873.7 mean versus 5634.9 median outside, dropping during high outfall flow.
pH stayed near neutral with mean 7.42 and max 7.64, well below 9, ruling out raw wastewater share.
Outfall flow averaged 74.8 versus 53.1 median outside, then fell back after the stretch.
Conductivity recovered to mean 5720.1 after the excess, confirming the low-conductivity episode ended.
Power matched expected load with observed 0.99 of expected and zero share outside band, showing aeration ran.

final.scope_line: Based on intake, ETP inflow, power, outfall flow, pH and conductivity and tank level for 2026-10-13 10:00 to 2026-10-14 14:00. Does not measure every pollutant.
limitations: No lab BOD result covers the interval, so organic pollutant removal cannot be shown by sampling.
No meter photos cover the interval, so meter accuracy rests on separate signals and replay checks.
Logbook claim of normal operation is a factory claim, not physical evidence.
Conductivity and flow show water routing, not every pollutant.

result.note: ETP balance: treated flow reaching the outfall vs outfall flow (same time). Boundary balance: intake vs outfall + losses + sludge water + tank storage change (reuse cancels). Tank balance: wastewater arriving (estimated from intake) vs ETP inflow + storage change; unaccounted water left the tank another way, or was intake water that never became wastewater. null means a required signal is under 80% coverage.
